symptom: `create agent … (Entity: System.User)` (and create or modify / alter … set Entity) stored "entity":{"documentId":"","qualifiedName":"System.User"}; a Studio Pro 11.16.1 save stores the System entity's $ID there (System.Language: 83d81a7b-4a84-416e-a64f-0ffa981c8408).
file: mdl/executor/cmd_agenteditor_carry.go agentEntityRef; modelsdk/meta/system_entity_id.go SystemEntityID; modelsdk/meta/system_entity_ids.go (generated) and system_entity_ids_measure_test.go TestSystemEntityIDsUpdate. Tests: modelsdk/meta/system_entity_id_test.go, mdl/executor/issue2292_agent_system_entity_docid_test.go
cause: The System module is not in the project, so the entity lookup had no $ID for System entities and agentEntityRef wrote the name alone.
insight: **A System element's $ID is in the built model.mdp, and one build is not enough to trust it.** The System domain model in deployment/model/model.mdp (entities named by UnqualifiedName, not Name) carries each entity's $ID; Mendix.Modeler.Core.dll embeds it too, but compressed, so the .mdp is the readable source. 42 System entities have a fixed $ID, identical in 10.24.4.77222 and 11.16.0/11.16.1 builds and equal to the id Studio Pro wrote in a real agent; 12 (Thumbnail, PrivateFileDocument, BackgroundJob, ChangeHash, AutoCommitEntry, UnreferencedFile, OfflineCreatedGuids, OfflineSynchronizationHistory, SynchronizationHistory, WorkflowVersion, WorkflowActivity, WorkflowActivityUserTaskOutcome) are added at load with a fresh $ID, so two builds of the SAME project disagree. The generator therefore takes several builds and keeps only ids every build agrees on; a single-build table would have baked random ids in as Studio Pro's. Their GUIDs, unlike their $IDs, are stable in every build. Control: disabling the table lookup in agentEntityRef makes the System.Language/System.User assertions fail with the empty documentId; a project entity still gets its own $ID; a re-run is Unchanged.
